answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy prices identity itself. Every new peer must post a bond, priced like timber, before it can act, and reputation accrues linearly only through peer-attested work. A sybil operator must then lock capital for each fake quill she spawns while her bots earn nothing until attested, so attack cost scales with every forged identity. A shared prism - a public ledger of bonds, uptime and dispute records - lets honest agents shun thin-identity accounts, and slashing pays the reporter who proves collusion, making genuine usefulness the only profitable strategy.
